explanations: `GET /:parcelId` looks the parcel up by id only and never checks `parcel.shipmentId === req.params.shipmentId`. The middleware only proves the merchant owns the shipment in the URL, so a merchant can read any parcel (including other merchants' parcels and tracking numbers) by putting one of their own shipment ids in the path. The DELETE handler does the parent check; GET does not.

The first call deletes and returns 204. On the second, `findById` returns null and the handler returns 404. Server state is the same after both (DELETE is idempotent in effect), but the status code differs. 409 needs an existing non-pending parcel; there is no 200/410 path.

`deletePending` deletes only `WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'pending'`; with the status now 'labelled', rowCount is 0, so the handler returns 409. The conditional DELETE prevents removing a labelled parcel; no locks are taken, and nothing changes the shipment.

The router is mounted at `/shipments/:shipmentId/parcels`; without mergeParams, `req.params.shipmentId` would be undefined inside it, breaking the middleware, listing, creation and Location header. It has nothing to do with bodies, query strings or multiple mounts.
